messages.subject: gl.run.structure
parts:
Hello,

I am having trouble using gl.run.structue. How to fix the following error?

Thank you in advance.

t1 <- gl.read.dart("C:/users/genom/downloads/SNP.csv",
                   ind.metafile = "C:/users/genom/downloads/SNP_metadata.csv" )

Completed: utils.read.dart 
Starting utils.dart2genlight 
Starting conversion....
Format is 2 rows.


sr <- gl.run.structure(t1, k.range = 2:5, num.k.rep = 3, 
exec = "C:/users/genom/downloads/structure_windows_console/console/structure.exe")



WARNING! Probable error in the input file.  
Individual 124, locus 136638;  encountered the following data 
"NA" when expecting an integer


WARNING! Probable error in the input file.  
Individual 124, locus 136638;  encountered the following data 
"NA" when expecting an integer

----------------------------------
There were errors in the input file (listed above). According to 
"mainparams" the input file should contain one row of markernames with 136637 entries,
 346 rows with 136640 entries .

There are 347 rows of data in the input file, with an average of 136639.99
entries per line.  The following shows the number of entries in each
line of the input file:

# Entries:   Line numbers
     136637:   1
     136640:   2--347
----------------------------------

Exiting the program due to error(s) listed above.

Error in FUN(X[[i]], ...) : 
  Error running STRUCTURE. Error code 1 returned.


Best regards,
Divya.

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: gl.run.structure
parts:
Hi Divya,

I suspect the problem comes from the name of your individuals. Please read the documentation of the function (see below) by typing in the R console: ?gl.run.structure

For this function to work, make sure that individual and population names have no spaces. To substitute spaces by underscores you could use the R function gsub as below.

popNames(gl) <- gsub(" ","_",popNames(gl))

indNames(gl) <- gsub(" ","_",indNames(gl))

It's also worth noting that Structure truncates individual names at 11 characters. The function will fail if the names of individuals are not unique after truncation. To avoid this possible problem, a number sequence, as shown in the code below, might be used instead of individual names. indNames(gl) <- as.character(1:length(indNames(gl)))


Cheers,
Luis
